data.name: Marketa
data.gender_notes: Marketa is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Czech name MARKYTÁ, which means ‘little Margrit’. This name is connected to the ancient Germanic name MARGARETE, which means ‘pearl’, and ultimately, to the name MARY. The name Marketa carries the meaning “Mary's little one” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Marketa usually hope their child will grow to embody mary's little one and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Marketa belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Mary's little one.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Marketa total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_hebrew.name: מרקא
in_hebrew.meaning: מרקא היא שמה של נערה חזקה ומוכשרת
in_hebrew.long_meaning: מרקא היא שמה של נערה חזקה ומוכשרת, שמקורה במרקוס, שפירושו פטיש או מקבת. השם מופיע בברית החדשה ומייצג דמות חשובה בכנסייה הנוצרית. השם מרקא הוא גרסה נשית של השם מרקוס, שפירושו המלט או הפטיש, ומייצג את האיכויות של החזקה והאמיצה.

in_greek.name: Μαργκέτα
in_greek.meaning: Μαργκέτα σημαίνει δυνατή και ικανή κοπέλα
in_greek.long_meaning: Μαργκέτα σημαίνει δυνατή και ικανή κοπέλα, που προέρχεται από το Μάρκος, που σημαίνει σφυρί ή πύλη. Το όνομα εμφανίζεται στη Νέα Διαθήκη και αντιπροσωπεύει μια σημαντική προσωπικότητα στην Εκκλησία. Το όνομα Μαργκέτα είναι η θηλυκή μορφή του ονόματος Μάρκος, που σημαίνει το σφυρί ή η πύλη, και αντιπροσωπεύει τις ιδιότητες της δυνατής και γενναίας.

Marketa, as a derivative of Mary, carries the spiritual weight of this reverence, symbolizing the grace, purity, and strength that Mary represents. Additionally, Marketa is associated with the zodiac sign Aries, further emphasizing her fierce and independent spirit.

historical_references.reference: Marketa Loketka, also known as Marketa of Magdeburg, was a Czech noblewoman, member of the famous Lusatian and Silesian Branch of the House of Wettin. She was born around 1262 and died around 1313. Marketa is best known for her role as a patroness of the Premonstratensian monastery at Magdeburg, Germany.

Marketa Krokska, also known as Marketa of Krumlov, was a Bohemian princess of the House of Rožmberk. She was born around 1467 and died around 1541. Marketa is best known for her role as a patron of the arts and learning, especially for her support of the University of Prague.
